name: Industry Surveys of AI Adoption
blurb: What surveys say about AI use in healthcare and life sciences.
title: Industry Surveys of AI Adoption
answer: Vendor and industry surveys show AI use is now the norm in life sciences. NVIDIA's 2025 survey of healthcare and life sciences organisations found most actively using AI and a large majority expecting it to transform the industry within three to five years, and Salesforce's 2025 survey found nearly all life sciences leaders expect AI agents to become essential.

crumbs.name: AI Adoption and Governance in Life Sciences

reading.body:
Surveys of life sciences organisations show AI use is already normal, with almost every leader expecting it to become more central.

Two vendor surveys from 2025 carry the claim. NVIDIA found 83 percent of healthcare and life sciences respondents agreeing AI will revolutionise the field within three to five years, and most organisations actively using it. Salesforce found nearly all life sciences leaders expect AI agents to become essential within two years. The pattern is expectation converging on certainty, and it is consistent across two independent sponsors.

For AI specifically, this matters because life sciences is a compute-heavy adopter. Drug discovery, genomics, and clinical data work all consume GPU capacity, so adoption in this sector translates into sustained demand for data centre space and power rather than a one-off experiment. The surveys do not measure that demand, and they do not measure outcomes.

What the data does not cover is the gap between intent and results. Both surveys report what respondents say they expect or are doing, not what they have measured. Vendor sponsorship is also a factor: NVIDIA sells the compute and Salesforce sells the agent platform, so each has an interest in the enthusiasm it reports. A leader should treat these as evidence of sentiment, not of deployed capability.

terms.line: The field of computer science dedicated to creating systems that perform tasks typically requiring human intelligence: understanding language, recognizing patterns, making decisions.

Models that create new content, text, images, video, audio, code, from patterns learned in training data. The 2022 shift from AI that classifies to AI that produces is what put this glossary on your reading list.

explainer:
Surveys from technology vendors, consultancies and industry groups regularly report high and rising AI adoption in health care and life sciences, along with strong expectations for agents and generative AI. They are useful for spotting trends and common priorities.

They also have limits. Many are run by companies that sell AI, samples are often self selected, questions measure intentions and perceptions rather than results, and definitions of use vary. Treat survey figures as indicators of sentiment and direction, and judge your own programme on measured outcomes.
